**Executive summary**

Paris is the capital and largest city of France, located on the Seine in the centre of the Île-de-France region [[s1]]. Its population within the city proper (the commune of Paris) is roughly 2.1 million: the official INSEE legal municipal population for the 2023 reference year is 2,103,778, in force as of 1 January 2026 [[s2]], and recent estimates show a slow decline to about 2.05–2.09 million [[s7]] [[s12]]. Broader definitions are substantially larger: the Paris metropolitan area (aire urbaine) has about 15.1 million inhabitants [[s6]], the Île-de-France region about 12.5 million [[s3]], and the Métropole du Grand Paris about 6.9 million [[s1]]. The "roughly 2.1 million" figure refers to the city proper; the wider region is on the order of 12–15 million depending on the definition used.

## The capital of France
Paris is the capital and largest city of France, with an estimated city population of about 2.04 million in an area of 105.4 km² as of January 2026 [[s1]]. It is located on the river Seine in the centre of the Île-de-France region and is the largest metropolitan area in the European Union [[s1]]. Administratively, Paris is both a commune and a department (INSEE code 75056), divided into twenty arrondissements [[s1]].

As the capital, Paris is the seat of France's national government: the President resides at the Élysée Palace, the Prime Minister at the Hôtel Matignon, and both houses of the French Parliament sit on the Rive Gauche — the Senate in the Palais du Luxembourg and the National Assembly in the Palais Bourbon [[s1]]. The city also hosts the headquarters of several international organisations, including UNESCO and the OECD [[s1]]. The capital status is not in dispute across any of the sources; the substantive question is the population figure, which varies by definition and reference date.

## Population of the city proper
The authoritative figure for the city proper comes from INSEE (Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques), France's national statistics institute. For the 2023 reference year, INSEE records a municipal population of 2,103,778 for the commune of Paris, a "counted separately" population of 15,634, and a total population of 2,119,412 [[s2]]. These reference populations entered into force on 1 January 2026 and were authenticated by decree n° 2025-1362 of 26 December 2025 [[s2]]. The municipal population is the figure used for statistical purposes; the total population is more often used for legislative or regulatory applications [[s2]].

Independent sources reproduce the same 2023 figure. Citypopulation.de, which cites INSEE as its source, lists 2,103,778 for the commune of Paris as of 1 January 2023 [[s4]] [[s11]]. INSEE's own dossier complet for the commune confirms 2,103,778 for 2023, alongside 2,187,526 for 2017 and 2,240,621 for 2012 [[s5]] [[s10]].

More recent estimates show a continuing decline. INSEE's Flash publication of October 2024 reports 2,087,600 people living in Paris in 2024, 45,500 fewer than three years earlier [[s7]]. The Wikipedia infobox and the EU city list both give 2,047,602 for 1 January 2026 [[s1]] [[s12]], and the European cities list gives 2,048,472 for 1 January 2025 [[s9]]. One Wikipedia passage gives 2,102,650 for January 2023 [[s1]], a figure slightly below the INSEE legal population of 2,103,778 for the same reference year — a small discrepancy likely reflecting different estimation methods (annual estimates versus the census-based legal population), but immaterial to the "roughly 2.1 million" answer.

The figures are summarised below:

| INSEE legal municipal population | 2,103,778 | 2023 reference year, in force 1 Jan 2026 [[s2]] |
| INSEE total population (municipal + counted separately) | 2,119,412 | 2023 reference year [[s2]] |
| INSEE Flash estimate | 2,087,600 | 2024 [[s7]] |

All of these fall within "roughly 2.1 million" for the city proper. The differences among them reflect the documented ongoing population decline rather than any contradiction among sources.

## Broader definitions: metropolitan area and region
The population figure depends heavily on which boundary is used, and the sources are explicit that the city proper is much smaller than the urbanised area around it. The Paris metropolitan area (aire urbaine, as of the 2020 revision) covers 1,929 communes and 18,941 km², with a population of 15,064,617 [[s6]]. This statistical area describes the reach of commuter movement to and from Paris and extends beyond the administrative Île-de-France region into nine surrounding departments [[s6]]. Paris itself, at 2,165,423, is the largest city within it [[s6]].

Two other definitions are commonly cited. The Métropole du Grand Paris, an administrative structure for cooperation between Paris and its nearest suburbs created in January 2016, covers 814 km² and had a population of 6.945 million in 2015 [[s1]]. The Île-de-France region, the administrative region containing Paris, had a population of 12,463,067 as of January 2023, or 18.3 percent of the population of France [[s3]]. INSEE's Flash publication notes that Paris accounts for 17 percent of the Île-de-France population on less than 1 percent of the regional territory [[s7]].

These are not conflicting figures but different scopes: the city proper (~2.1 million), the Grand Paris cooperation structure (~6.9 million), the region (~12.5 million), and the broader commuter-based metropolitan area (~15.1 million). A reader asking for "the population of Paris" should be aware that the answer ranges from about 2.1 million to about 15 million depending on the boundary chosen; the city proper is the standard referent for "the capital."

## Population trend and density
Paris's population has been declining for decades, which explains the small differences among the figures cited above. The city reached a historic high of 2.9 million in 1921, then declined at every census between 1954 and 1999, falling to 2,125,246 in 1999 [[s3]]. INSEE's official series shows 2,590,771 in 1968 falling to 2,103,778 in 2023, with a mid-2000s rebound to 2,240,621 in 2012 [[s2]] [[s5]]. The decline resumed after 2012: the average annual change was −0.5 percent from 2012 to 2017 and −0.6 percent from 2017 to 2023 [[s8]].

INSEE attributes the recent decline to a negative migration balance. From 2015 to 2021, the excess of births over deaths contributed +0.6 percent per year, but the migration deficit reduced the population by 1.2 percent per year, and the natural surplus did not compensate for the migration loss [[s7]]. The migration deficit applies to all age groups except 18–24-year-olds, reflecting annual arrivals of young workers and students [[s7]]. INSEE projects that if current trends continue, Paris would have 82,000 fewer residents in 2040 than in 2020, reaching about 2,064,000 [[s7]].

Paris is also the most densely populated city in France, with about 19,900 inhabitants per km² in 2024 [[s7]]. INSEE's census data give an average density of 19,959.9 inhabitants per km² for 2023 [[s5]]. Historically, according to Eurostat, the Commune of Paris was the most densely populated city in the European Union in 2012, with 21,616 people per square kilometre within the city limits [[s3]]. Density is highest in the northern and eastern arrondissements; the 11th arrondissement had a density of 40,672 inhabitants per km² in 1999 [[s3]].

## Data sources and reliability
The population figures rest on a single authoritative source: INSEE, whose reference populations are census-based, updated annually, and authenticated by decree [[s2]]. The 2023 reference populations were calculated according to the concepts defined in decree n° 2003-485 of 5 June 2003, as modified, and were authenticated by decree n° 2025-1362 of 26 December 2025 [[s2]]. INSEE notes that because of the Covid-19 health crisis, the annual census survey scheduled for 2021 was postponed to 2022, and INSEE adapted its calculation methods to continue producing reference populations of quality each year [[s2]].

Independent aggregators reproduce INSEE figures: citypopulation.de lists 2,103,778 for 2023, citing INSEE as its source [[s4]] [[s11]]. The Wikipedia figures, including the 2,047,602 figure for January 2026, are consistent with the INSEE series and the documented decline [[s1]] [[s12]]. The Wikipedia Demographics article carries a notice that parts of its statistics sections need updating as of January 2018 [[s3]], so its older figures should be treated with more caution than the INSEE data; the more recent figures it reports, however, match the INSEE series.

One caveat applies to the density figures: the INSEE English-language dossier for the municipality contains a figure of "1,995,994.3 inhabitants per square kilometre" for 2023 [[s10]], which is a transcription error — the French-language dossier gives 19,959.9 for the same year [[s5]], and INSEE's Flash publication gives about 19,900 for 2024 [[s7]]. The 19,959.9 figure is the correct one and is used here.

## Conclusion
The question has a straightforward answer: the capital of France is Paris, and its population is roughly 2.1 million within the city proper. The most authoritative figure is INSEE's legal municipal population of 2,103,778 for the 2023 reference year, in force 1 January 2026 [[s2]], with more recent estimates showing a slow decline to about 2.05 million by early 2026 [[s1]] [[s12]]. The "roughly" in the question is comfortably satisfied by every figure in the evidence pool.

The main qualification a reader should carry away is definitional. "Paris" can mean the commune (about 2.1 million), the Grand Paris cooperation structure (about 6.9 million), the Île-de-France region (about 12.5 million), or the commuter-based metropolitan area (about 15.1 million) [[s1]] [[s3]] [[s6]]. The sources are consistent within each definition, and the differences among the city-proper figures are explained by the documented, ongoing population decline driven by a negative migration balance [[s7]]. No evidence in the pool contradicts the capital status or the approximate population; the only unresolved point is which boundary the questioner intends, and the answer above gives the city proper as the standard referent while flagging the alternatives.

You are writing a complete analytical research report answering one question from an assembled evidence pool.

Question: What is the capital of France and roughly its population?

REFERENCE DATE (UTC, original user request): 2026-09-08. Use an explicitly requested historical or future date when the task gives one. For current recommendations, check whether dated observations still apply; distinguish current deployment from historical conditions and projections.

Researcher's brief (how the question was read and what was investigated):
Simple factual question: capital of France is Paris; approximate population. Both core angles are banked and cross-validated across INSEE official pages, citypopulation.de, and multiple Wikipedia articles. City proper (commune of Paris): official INSEE legal municipal population 2,103,778 for the 2023 reference year (in force 1 Jan 2026); INSEE total population 2,119,412; INSEE Flash (Oct 2024) gives 2,087,600 for 2024; EU city list shows 2,047,602 for 1 Jan 2026 — all within 'roughly 2.1 million', reflecting the documented slow decline. Broader definitions: Paris metropolitan area (aire urbaine) 15,064,617 (2020 boundaries, 18,941 km²); Métropole du Grand Paris ~6.945 million (2015); Paris is 17% of the Île-de-France regional population. Host requires 5+ evidence-backed angles; I am expanding coverage to include the broader-region, population-trend, density, and data-source angles, all supportable from the 12 admitted sources already in the pool. No further retrieval needed.

COVERAGE MAP (research state; use as guidance, not as a required outline):
Covered angles:
- Capital city of France and its identity (evidence: web_a3a9f50070e962dd5455cca3, web_912639947b6e30334cd63f59)
  Finding: Paris is the capital and largest city of France, located on the Seine in the centre of the Île-de-France region; INSEE commune code 75056. It is the seat of the national government (President at Élysée Palace, Prime Minister at Hôtel Matignon, Parliament on the Rive Gauche).
- Approximate population of the capital, city proper (commune of Paris), with date (evidence: web_912639947b6e30334cd63f59, web_dcbb48919474a2c200cc3162, web_4b9a68f2101be4b45f3c9513, web_e097d1b03a742e9b3a3b897a, web_65e4e5164565458316c7430b)
  Finding: Official INSEE legal municipal population 2,103,778 for the 2023 reference year (in force 1 Jan 2026); INSEE total population (municipal + counted separately) 2,119,412. Independently confirmed by citypopulation.de (2,103,778, 2023, sourced from INSEE) and the Wikipedia Demographics article. Recent estimates show a slow decline: INSEE Flash (Oct 2024) gives 2,087,600 for 2024, and the EU city list shows 2,047,602 for 1 Jan 2026 — all consistent with 'roughly 2.1 million' for the city proper.
- Broader definitions: metropolitan area and region population (evidence: web_a02c4c9a3a1d6ab86978fe0b, web_e097d1b03a742e9b3a3b897a, web_a3a9f50070e962dd5455cca3)
  Finding: The Paris metropolitan area (aire urbaine, 2020 boundaries: 1,929 communes, 18,941 km²) has a population of 15,064,617, with Paris (2,165,423) as the largest city. The Métropole du Grand Paris (2015) had 6.945 million over 814 km². Paris accounts for 17% of the Île-de-France regional population on less than 1% of the regional territory, implying a regional population of roughly 12 million. So 'roughly 2.1 million' refers to the city proper; the wider region/metro area is on the order of 12–15 million depending on definition.
- Population trend: Paris is declining (evidence: web_e097d1b03a742e9b3a3b897a, web_912639947b6e30334cd63f59)
  Finding: Paris has been losing residents for decades. INSEE's official series shows 2,590,771 (1968) falling to 2,103,778 (2023), with a mid-2000s rebound. INSEE Flash (Oct 2024) reports 2,087,600 in 2024, 45,500 fewer than three years earlier, driven by a negative migration balance that the natural surplus does not offset; if trends continue, Paris would have 82,000 fewer residents in 2040 than in 2020. This decline explains the small differences among the population figures cited.
- Density of the capital (evidence: web_e097d1b03a742e9b3a3b897a, web_dcbb48919474a2c200cc3162)
  Finding: Paris has the highest population density in France, about 19,900 inhabitants per km² (2024, INSEE Flash). Historically it was the most densely populated city in the EU (21,616/km² in 2012 per Eurostat), with the 11th arrondissement reaching 40,672/km² in 1999. Density is highest in the northern and eastern arrondissements.
- Data source and reliability of the population figures (evidence: web_912639947b6e30334cd63f59, web_4b9a68f2101be4b45f3c9513)
  Finding: The authoritative source is INSEE (Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques), whose reference populations are census-based, updated annually, and authenticated by decree (e.g., décret n° 2025-1362 of 26 Dec 2025 for the 2023 reference year, in force 1 Jan 2026). The 'roughly' tolerance in the question is comfortably met by all cited figures.

- Population figures cross-validated across INSEE official pages, citypopulation.de, and Wikipedia; the 2,103,778 (2023 legal) vs 2,047,602 (1 Jan 2026 estimate) difference is explained by the documented ongoing population decline and is within the 'roughly' tolerance. Paris[[a]](#cite_note-7) is the [capital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_city) and [largest city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_communes_in_France_with_over_20,000_inhabitants) of [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France), with an estimated city population of 2.04 million in an area of 105.4 km2 (40.7 sq mi), as of January 2026[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paris&action=edit),[[4]](#cite_note-Pop.Paris-4) and a metropolitan population of 13.3 million (2023). Located on the river [Seine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seine) in the centre of the [Île-de-France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Île-de-France) region, it is the [largest metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_metropolitan_areas_in_Europe) and [fourth-most populous city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_the_European_Union_by_population_within_city_limits) in the [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union) (EU). Paris is nicknamed the "City of Light", partly because of its role in the [Age of Enlightenment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Age_of_Enlightenment).
Administratively, Paris is divided into [twenty arrondissements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrondissements_of_Paris) (districts), each having their own cultural identity. [Haussmann's renovation of Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haussmann's_renovation_of_Paris), which created new boulevards, parks, and public works, gave birth to a modern city known as the "[capital of the 19th century](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris,_Capital_of_the_19th_Century)". Paris is a major railway, motorway, and air-transport hub; in 2024 [Charles de Gaulle Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_de_Gaulle_Airport) was the EU's [busiest airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_the_busiest_airports_in_Europe). Paris has one of the most [sustainable transportation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sustainable_transportation) systems in the world and is one of only two cities that have received the [Sustainable Transport Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sustainable_Transport_Award) twice. Its [Art Nouveau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Nouveau)-decorated [Métro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Métro) has become a symbol of the city. Paris is known for its museums and architectural landmarks: the [Musée d'Orsay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musée_d'Orsay), [Musée Marmottan Monet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musée_Marmottan_Monet), and [Musée de l'Orangerie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musée_de_l'Orangerie) are noted for their collections of French [Impressionist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impressionism) art, while the [Musée National d'Art Moderne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musée_National_d'Art_Moderne), [Musée Rodin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musée_Rodin), and [Musée Picasso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musée_Picasso) are noted for their collections of [modern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_art) and [contemporary art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_art). Parts of the city along the [Seine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seine) have been designated as a [UNESCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO) [World Heritage Site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Heritage_Site) since 1991[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paris&action=edit).
The [president of France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_France) and both houses of the [French Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Parliament) sit in Paris. Paris is home to several [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations) organisations, including [UNESCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO), as well as other international organisations such as the [OECD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OECD), the [International Bureau of Weights and Measures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Bureau_of_Weights_and_Measures) (in neighbouring [Saint-Cloud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Cloud)), the [International Energy Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Energy_Agency), the [Organisation internationale de la Francophonie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organisation_internationale_de_la_Francophonie), the [International Federation for Human Rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Federation_for_Human_Rights), and the [Fédération internationale de l'Automobile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fédération_Internationale_de_l'Automobile), along with European bodies such as the [European Space Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Space_Agency), the [European Banking Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Banking_Authority), and the [European Securities and Markets Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Securities_and_Markets_Authority). The city [hosts many sporting events](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sport_in_Paris), such as the [French Open](https://en.wikipe

city's first mayor since 1871 and only the fourth since 1794. The current mayor is [Emmanuel Grégoire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmanuel_Grégoire), a member of the [Socialist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socialist_Party_(France)), who was elected in [2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Paris_municipal_election).[[110]](#cite_note-112)The [Hôtel de Ville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hôtel_de_Ville,_Paris), or city hall
The mayor of Paris is [elected indirectly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indirect_election) by Paris voters. The voters of each of the city's 20 arrondissements elect members to the [Conseil de Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conseil_de_Paris) (Council of Paris), which elects the mayor. The council is composed of 163 members. Each arrondissement is allocated many seats, dependent upon its population, from 10 members for each of the least-populated arrondissements to 34 members for the most populated. The council is elected using [closed list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Closed_list) [proportional representation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proportional_representation) in a [two-round system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two-round_system).[[111]](#cite_note-Election_Code_–_Article_L260-113)
Party lists winning an absolute [majority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Majority) in the first round – or at least a [plurality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plurality_(voting)) in the second round – automatically win half the seats of an arrondissement. The remaining half of the seats are distributed proportionally to all lists which win at least 5% of the vote, using the [highest averages method](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highest_averages_method).[[111]](#cite_note-Election_Code_–_Article_L260-113) This ensures that the winning party or coalition always wins a majority of the seats, even if they do not win an absolute majority of the vote.[[112]](#cite_note-Pariscouncil-114)
Before the [2020 Paris municipal election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Paris_municipal_election), each of Paris's 20 arrondissements had its own town hall and a directly elected council ([conseil d'arrondissement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conseil_d'arrondissement)), which elects an arrondissement mayor.[[113]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShales200716-115) The council of each arrondissement is composed of members of the Conseil de Paris, and members who serve only on the council of the arrondissement. The number of deputy mayors in each arrondissement varies depending on its population. As of 1996, there were 20 arrondissement mayors and 120 deputy mayors.[[109]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFierro1996334-111) The creation of [Paris Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Centre), a unified administrative division with a single mayor covering the first four arrondissements, took effect with the said 2020 election. The other 16 arrondissements continue to have their own mayors.[[114]](#cite_note-116)

### Métropole du Grand Paris
A map of the Greater Paris Metropolis and its governing territories
In January 2016, the [Métropole du Grand Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Paris) came into existence.[[115]](#cite_note-MGP-117) It is an administrative structure for co-operation between the City of Paris and its nearest suburbs. It includes the City of Paris, plus the communes of the three departments of the inner suburbs, [Hauts-de-Seine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hauts-de-Seine), [Seine-Saint-Denis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seine-Saint-Denis) and [Val-de-Marne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Val-de-Marne), plus seven communes in the outer suburbs, including [Argenteuil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argenteuil) in [Val d'Oise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Val_d'Oise) and [Paray-Vieille-Poste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paray-Vieille-Poste) in [Essonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Essonne), which were added to include the major airports of Paris. The Metropole covers 814 km2 (314 sq mi). In 2015, it had a population of 6.945 million people.[[116]](#cite_note-118)[[117]](#cite_note-lemoniteur1-119)
The new structure is administered by a Metropolitan Council of 210 members, not directly elected, but chosen by the councils of the member Communes. By 2020, its basic competencies will include urban planning, housing, and protection of the environment.[[115]](#cite_note-MGP-117)[[117]](#cite_note-lemoniteur1-119) In January 2016, [Patrick Ollier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Ollier) was elected the first president of the metropolitan council. Though the Metropole has a population of nearly seven million people and accounts for 25 percent of the GDP of France, it has a very small budget: just 65 million Euros, compared with eight billion Euros for the City of Paris.[[118]](#cite_note-120)

### Regional government

The [Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Region) of [Île de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Île_de_France), including Paris and its surrounding communities, is governed by the [Regional Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regional_Council_of_Île-de-France), composed of 209 members representing the different communes. In December 2015, a list of candidates of the Union of the Right, a coalition of centrist and right-wing parties, led by [Valérie Pécresse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valérie_Pécresse), narrowly won the regional election, defeating a coalition of Socialists and ecologists. The Socialists had governed the region for seventeen years. The regional council has 121 members from the Union of the Right, 66 from the Union of the Left and 22 from the extreme right National Front.[[119]](#cite_note-121)

### National government
The [Élysée Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Élysée_Palace), official residence of the [President of France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_France)
As the capital of France, Paris is the seat of France's [national government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_France). For the executive, the two chief officers each have their own official residences, which also serve as their offices. The [President of the French Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_France) resides at the [Élysée Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Élysée_Palace).[[120]](#cite_note-122) The [Prime Minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_France)'s seat is at the [Hôtel Matignon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hôtel_Matignon).[[121]](#cite_note-123)[[122]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKnappWright200693–94-124) Government ministries are located in various parts of the city, many near the Hôtel Matignon.[[123]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBorrus2012288-125)
Both houses of the [French Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Parliament) are located on the Rive Gauche. The upper house, the [Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senate_(France)), meets in the [Palais du Luxembourg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palais_du_Luxembourg). The more important lower house, the [National Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Assembly_(France)), meets in the [Palais Bourbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palais_Bourbon). The [President of the Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_the_Senate_of_France), the second-highest public official in France, with the President of the Republic being the sole superior, resides in the [Petit Luxembourg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petit_Luxembourg), a smaller palace annexe to the Palais du Luxembourg.[[124]](#cite_note-126)The Palais-Royal, residence of the [Conseil d'État](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conseil_d'État_(France))
France's highest courts are located in Paris. The [Court of Cassation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Court_of_Cassation_(France)), the highest court in the judicial order, which reviews criminal and civil cases, is located in the [Palais de Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palais_de_Justice,_Paris) on the Île de la Cité.[[125]](#cite_note-127) The [Conseil d'État](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_of_State_(France)), which provides legal advice to the executive and acts as the highest court in the administrative order, judging litigation against public bodies, is located in the [Palais-Royal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palais-Royal) in the [1st arrondissement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1st_arrondissement_of_Paris).[[126]](#cite_note-128) The [Constitutional Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitutional_Council_of_France), an advisory body with ultimate authority on the constitutionality of laws and government decrees, meets in the Montpensier wing of the Palais Royal.[[127]](#cite_note-129)
Paris and its region host the headquarters of several international organisations, including [UNESCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO), the [Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organisation_for_Economic_Co-operation_and_Development), the [International Chamber of Commerce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Chamber_of_Commerce), the [Paris Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Club), the [European Space Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Space_Agency), the [International Energy Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Energy_Agency), the [Organisation internationale de la Francophonie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organisation_internationale_de_la_Francophonie), the [European Union Institute for Security Studies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union_Institute_for_Security_Studies), the [International Bureau of Weights and Measures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Bureau_of_Weights_and_Measures), the [International Exhibition Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bureau_of_International_Expositions), and the [International Federation for Human Rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Federation_for_Human_Rights).

## Définitions

Le terme générique de « populations de référence » regroupe pour chaque commune sa
                        population municipale, sa population comptée à part et sa population totale qui est
                        la somme des deux précédentes.
Les populations de référence sont définies par le décret n°2003-485 publié au Journal
                        officiel du 8 juin 2003, relatif au recensement de la population, modifié par le décret
                        n° 2019-1302 du 5 décembre 2019. Désormais, elles sont actualisées et authentifiées
                        par un décret chaque année. Environ 350 textes législatifs ou réglementaires font
                        référence à ces populations.
La population municipale est celle qui est utilisée à des fins statistiques ; la population
                        totale est la plus souvent utilisée pour l'application de dispositions législatives
                        ou réglementaires.

The city of [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris) (also called the Commune or Department of Paris) had a population of 2,047,602 people within its administrative city limits as of 1 January 2026.[[1]](#cite_note-paris_pop_2023-1) It is surrounded by the Paris [unité urbaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unité_urbaine), or urban area, the [most populous urban area in the European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Largest_urban_areas_of_the_European_Union).
In 2023 the unité urbaine had a population of 11,013,774 in 2,824 km2 (1,090 sq mi).[[2]](#cite_note-pop-2) The Paris Region, or [Île-de-France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Île-de-France), covers 12,012 km2 (4,638 sq mi), and has its own regional council and president. It has a population of 12,463,067 as of January 2023, or 18.3 percent of the population of France.[[2]](#cite_note-pop-2) The metropolitan or [functional area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Functional_area_(France)) (aire d'attraction) of Paris covers 18,941 km2 (7,313 sq mi) and has 13,320,752 inhabitants (2023).[[2]](#cite_note-pop-2)
The population of the city of Paris reached a historic high of 2.9 million in 1921 but then declined; between 1954 and 1999 it declined at every census, falling to 2,125,246 in 1999.[[3]](#cite_note-3) After that it began to climb again, reaching 2,240,621 in 2012, but falling to 2,103,778 in 2023.[[1]](#cite_note-paris_pop_2023-1)
The city's population loss reflected the experience of most other core cities in the developed world that have not expanded their boundaries. The principal factors in the process were a significant decline in household size, and a dramatic migration of residents to the suburbs between 1962 and 1975.  Factors in the migration included [deindustrialisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deindustrialization), high rent, the [gentrification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gentrification) of many inner quarters, the transformation of living space into offices, and greater affluence among working families. The city's population loss was one of the most severe among international municipalities and the largest for any that had achieved more than 2,000,000 residents. Since then, an influx of younger residents and immigrants has contributed to the growth of the city.

## Density
[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Demographics_of_Paris&action=edit&section=1)]Paris population pyramid in 2022
According to [Eurostat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurostat), the EU statistical agency, in 2012 the Commune of Paris was the most densely populated city in the European Union, with 21,616 people per square kilometre within the city limits (the NUTS-3 statistical area),  ahead of Inner London West, which had 10,374 persons per square kilometre.  According to the same census, three departments bordering Paris, [Hauts-de-Seine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hauts-de-Seine), [Seine-Saint-Denis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seine-Saint-Denis) and [Val-de-Marne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Val-de-Marne), had population densities of over ten thousand persons per square kilometre, ranking among the ten most densely populated areas of the EU.[[4]](#cite_note-4)
Paris is one of the most densely populated cities in the world.[[5]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMadgeWillmott200611-5) Its density, excluding the outlying woodland parks of [Boulogne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bois_de_Boulogne) and [Vincennes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bois_de_Vincennes), was 24,448 inhabitants per square kilometre (63,320/sq mi) in the 1999 official census, which could be compared only with some [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia) [megapolises](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megalopolis_(city_type)) and the [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City) [borough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borough_(New_York_City)) of [Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan). Even including the two woodland areas, its population density was 20,755/km2 (53,760/sq mi) in 2017,[[6]](#cite_note-compparis-6) the sixth-most-densely populated commune in France after [Levallois-Perret](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levallois-Perret), [Vincennes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vincennes), [Le Pré-Saint-Gervais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le_Pré-Saint-Gervais), [Saint-Mandé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Mandé) and [Montrouge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montrouge), all of which border the city proper.[[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed)]
The most sparsely populated quarters are the western and central office and administration-focused [arrondissements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrondissements_of_Paris). The city's population is densest in the northern and eastern arrondissements; the [11th arrondissement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/11th_arrondissement_of_Paris) had a density of 40,672 inhabitants per square kilometre (105,340/sq mi) in 1999, and some of the same arrondissement's eastern quarters had densities close to 100,000/km2 (260,000/sq mi) in the same year.Population density map of Paris in January 2017

## Paris agglomeration
[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Demographics_of_Paris&action=edit&section=2)]
The city of Paris covers an area much smaller than the urban area of which it is the core. At present, Paris's real urbanisation, defined by the [pôle urbain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pôle_urbain) (urban cluster) statistical area, covers 2,845 km2 (1,098 sq mi),[[8]](#cite_note-UU_superficie-8) or an area about 27 times larger than the city itself. The administration of Paris's urban growth is divided between itself and its surrounding departments: Paris's closest ring of three adjoining departments, or petite couronne ("small ring") are fully saturated with urban growth, and the ring of four departments outside of these, the grande couronne departments, are only covered in their inner regions by Paris's urbanisation. These eight departments form the larger administrative Île-de-France région; most of this region is filled, and overextended in places, by the Paris [functional area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Functional_area), which, in 2023, was populated by over 13 million people.[[9]](#cite_note-pop_AAV-9)
The Paris agglomeration has shown a steady rate of growth since the end of the late 16th century [French Wars of Religion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Wars_of_Religion), save brief setbacks during the French Revolution and World War II. With 13.3 million inhabitants in 2023, the annual population growth rate of the Paris functional area was between 0.4% and 1.0% over the past 55 years.[[9]](#cite_note-pop_AAV-9)

By law, French censuses do not ask questions regarding ethnicity or religion, but do gather information concerning one's country of birth. From this it is still possible to determine that Paris and its metropolitan area is one of the most multi-cultural in Europe: According to the 2011 census, 456,105 residents of the municipality of Paris, or 20.3 percent,  and 2,117,901 residents of the Paris Region (Île-de-France), or 17.9 percent, were born outside France.[[12]](#cite_note-12)  At the 1999 census, 4.2% of the population in Paris [metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Area_(France)) were recent immigrants (people who had immigrated to France between 1990 and 1999), the majority from [Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia) and [Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Africa). 37 % of all immigrants in France live in the Paris region.[[13]](#cite_note-riot-13)
The first wave of international migration to Paris started as early as 1820, with the arrivals of German peasants fleeing an agricultural crisis in their homeland. Several waves of immigration followed continually until today: Italians and central European Jews during the 19th century; Russians after the [revolution of 1917](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Revolution_of_1917) and Armenians fleeing [genocide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armenian_genocide) in the Ottoman Empire;[[14]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHassell199122-14) colonial subjects during [World War I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I) and later;[[15]](#cite_note-15) Poles between the two world wars; Spaniards, Italians, Portuguese, and North Africans from the 1950s to the 1970s; North African Jews after colonies in that region gained independence; Africans and Asians since then.[[16]](#cite_note-past_immigration-16)
The Paris metropolitan region, or aire urbaine, is estimated to be home to some 1.7 million Muslims, who comprise between 10–15 per cent of the area's population. However, without official data, the margin of error of these estimates is extremely high as it is based on one's country of birth (someone born in a Muslim country or born to a parent from a Muslim country is considered as a "potential Muslim").[[17]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEZarkaTaussigFleury200427-17) According to the North American Jewish Data Bank, an estimated 310,000 Jews also live in Paris and the surrounding Île-de-France region, an area with a population of 11.7 million. Paris has historically been a magnet for immigrants, and it hosts one of the largest concentrations of immigrants in Europe today.[[18]](#cite_note-18)

### Immigrants and their children in departments of Île-de-France (Paris Region)
[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Demographics_of_Paris&action=edit&section=4)]
According to the National Institute for Statistics and Economic Studies, responsible for the production and analysis of official statistics in France, 20 per cent of people living in the city of Paris are immigrants, and 41.3 per cent of people under 20 have at least one immigrant parent.[[19]](#cite_note-19) Among the young people under 18, 12.1 per cent are of [Maghrebi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maghrebis) origin, 9.9 per cent of [Subsaharan African](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subsaharan_Africa) origin, and 4.0 per cent of [South European](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Europe) origin.[[20]](#cite_note-20)  In 2020–2021, about 6 million people, or 49% of the population of [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Île-de-France_(region)), are either immigrants (21%) or have at least one immigrant parent (28%). These figures do not include French people born in [Overseas France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overseas_France) and their direct descendants.[[21]](#cite_note-21)

### Africans
[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Demographics_of_Paris&action=edit&section=7)]
Main article: [Sub-Saharan African community of Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sub-Saharan_African_community_of_Paris)
Main article: [Maghrebian community of Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maghrebian_community_of_Paris)
As of 2012 tens of thousands of people of African origins live in Paris. This group includes those born in France who had African parents and naturalized French citizens born in Africa. The majority come from the [Maghreb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maghreb), including [Algeria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algeria), [Morocco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morocco), and [Tunisia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tunisia). Other countries with populations in Paris include [Burkina Faso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burkina_Faso), the [Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_the_Congo), [Guinea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guinea), [Mali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mali), and [Senegal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senegal).[[23]](#cite_note-23)

### Asians
[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Demographics_of_Paris&action=edit&section=8)]
As of 1998 [Île-de-France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Île-de-France) has half of the Asian population of France.[[24]](#cite_note-Guillonp186-24) As of 1990 the majority of Asians living in France are [ethnic Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Chinese) originating from several countries.[[25]](#cite_note-Guillonp187-25)
In 1974 France stopped allowing foreign workers into its borders. The Asian population of France increased despite the closure. In 1975 there were 20,000 Asians in Île-de-France. In 1982 the region had 59,000. This increased to 108,000 in 1990.[[25]](#cite_note-Guillonp187-25)
In France the "Asians" are defined as people originating from the [East Asian cultural sphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Asian_cultural_sphere). The term does not include people from the [Indian subcontinent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_subcontinent).[[24]](#cite_note-Guillonp186-24)

#### Geography of the Asian population
[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Demographics_of_Paris&action=edit&section=9)]
For the entire [Île-de-France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Île-de-France) region, there were a total of 108,511 persons who held or formerly held Cambodian, Chinese, Laotian, Taiwanese, and Vietnamese citizenships as of 1990. This included 64,361 current citizens of those countries and 44,150 former citizens who became naturalized as French citizens.[[26]](#cite_note-Guillonp188-26)
As of 1990, there were a combined total of 31,773 persons who held or formerly held Cambodian, Chinese, Laotian, Taiwanese, and Vietnamese citizenships in the City of [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris). This included 21,655 current citizens of those countries and 10,118 former citizens who became naturalized as French citizens.[[26]](#cite_note-Guillonp188-26)
As of 1990 fewer than 10,000 persons of East/Southeast Asian origin resided in six communes of [Marne-la-Vallée](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marne-la-Vallée). 26% of the population of [Lognes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lognes) was Asian, and other percentages were 8% in [Noisiel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noisiel), 5–6% in [Noisy-le-Grand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noisy-le-Grand), and 5–6% in [Torcy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torcy,_Seine-et-Marne). In 1982 there were 6,000 Asians in Marne-la-Vallée, making up 3–4% of the area's population. In 1987 the number increased to 9,000.[[27]](#cite_note-Guillonp198-27)
As of circa 1998 [Ivry-sur-Seine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivry-sur-Seine) and [Vitry-sur-Seine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitry-sur-Seine) had a combined Asian population of 3,600.[[28]](#cite_note-Guillonp197-28)
As of circa 1998 there were about 6,000 East/Southeast Asians in and around [Aulnay-sous-Bois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aulnay-sous-Bois), and there were 3,000 persons of East and Southeast Asian origin in Aulnay proper. Most of them were of [Cambodian origin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambodian_French), including those with and without Cambodian citizenship. The commune also had an above-average number of [persons of Laotian origin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laotians_in_France), including those with and without Laotian citizenship. Ethnicities included [Khmer people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khmer_people), [Lao people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lao_people), and [Overseas Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overseas_Chinese).[[28]](#cite_note-Guillonp197-28)

#### Cambodians
[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Demographics_of_Paris&action=edit&section=10)]
As of 1990, in the City of Paris there were 7,950 Cambodian citizens and 3,279 former Cambodian citizens who became naturalized as French. The combined total is 11,229.[[26]](#cite_note-Guillonp188-26)
That year, in the Île-de-France region there were 26,553 Cambodian citizens and 13,068 former Cambodian citizens naturalized as French. The combined total was 39,421.[[26]](#cite_note-Guillonp188-26)

#### Chinese
[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Demographics_of_Paris&action=edit&section=11)]

As of 1990 the majority of Asians living in the Paris area are [ethnic Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overseas_Chinese) originating from several countries.[[25]](#cite_note-Guillonp187-25) The largest group includes ethnic Chinese from [Indochina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indochina), and a smaller group originates from [Zhejiang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang).[[29]](#cite_note-Guillonp189-29)

As of 2013 the official number of Japanese residents in Paris was 16,277.[[30]](#cite_note-ConteHelmp81-30)

#### Laotians
[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Demographics_of_Paris&action=edit&section=13)]
As of 1990, in the City of Paris there were 2,185 Laotian citizens and 1,376 former Laotian citizens naturalized as French, making a combined total of 3,561.[[26]](#cite_note-Guillonp188-26)
As of that year, in the Île-de-France region there were 10,110 Laotian citizens and 8,177 former Laotian citizens, making a combined total of 18,287.[[26]](#cite_note-Guillonp188-26)

#### Vietnamese
[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Demographics_of_Paris&action=edit&section=14)]
Main article: [Vietnamese community in Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnamese_community_in_Paris)
In periods before 1975 several Vietnamese arrived in Paris, including intellectuals, those who worked as civil servants in colonial times, and those who came to Paris to study and did not return home. Ethnic Vietnamese arriving after 1975 became a part of an ethnic network established by those that came before them. Many Vietnamese achieved proficiency in the medical, scientific, and computer science fields.[[31]](#cite_note-Guillonp190-31)
As of 1990, in the City of Paris there were 3,802 Vietnamese citizens and 4,155 former Vietnamese citizens naturalized as French, making a total of 7,957.[[26]](#cite_note-Guillonp188-26)
As of that year, in the Île-de-France region there were 16,387 Vietnamese citizens and 20,261 former Vietnamese citizens naturalized as French, making a total of 36,648.[[26]](#cite_note-Guillonp188-26)

## Champ

### Recensements de la population

Les données sont proposées aux utilisateurs notamment pour
                     comparer des communes, regrouper des modalités de variables ou obtenir
                     des résultats sur des ensembles personnalisés de communes.
Issues de calculs liés aux techniques d’échantillonnage, les
                     données en effectifs sont fournies avec plusieurs décimales ; celles-ci
                     doivent être utilisées pour tous les calculs réalisés, de façon à éviter
                     les erreurs d’arrondis.
Pour avoir plus d’information sur le recensement de la
                     population, consultez la page de [présentation du recensement de la
                        population](/fr/information/2383265).
Les données proviennent soit de l’exploitation principale
                     (princ), soit de l’exploitation complémentaire (compl).
Pour plus d’information méthodologique, vous pouvez consulter
                     les fiches ["Conseils pour
                        l’utilisation des résultats du recensement"](/fr/information/2383177).
Ces fiches présentent les caractéristiques du recensement de la
                     population et traitent de leurs conséquences sur l’utilisation des
                     données. Elles précisent en particulier les changements affectant les
                     principales variables statistiques et leur comparabilité avec les
                     recensements précédents.

### État civil

Les statistiques annuelles concernant les naissances
                     domiciliées sont dressées à partir des bulletins
                     statistiques de l’état civil, établis par les maires, au moment et dans
                     la commune où ont lieu les naissances. Elles portent sur les naissances
                     ayant eu lieu dans toutes les communes de France. Les naissances ayant
                     eu lieu à l’étranger ou dans les COM ne sont pas comptabilisées.
La variable "commune" correspond à la commune du domicile de la
                     mère en France.
Les statistiques comprennent les jugements déclaratifs de
                     naissance, mais ne prennent pas en compte les enfants mort-nés.

Les statistiques annuelles concernant les décès
                     domiciliés sont dressées à partir des bulletins
                     statistiques de l’état civil, établis par les maires, au moment et dans
                     la commune où ont lieu les décès. Elles portent sur les décès ayant eu
                     lieu dans toutes les communes de France. Les décès ayant eu lieu à
                     l’étranger ou dans les COM ne sont pas comptabilisés.
La variable "commune" correspond à la commune du domicile du
                     défunt en France.
Les statistiques comprennent les jugements déclaratifs de décès.

### Fichier Localisé Social et Fiscal (Filosofi)

Le champ porte sur les personnes appartenant à des ménages
                     fiscaux ordinaires dont le revenu disponible est positif ou nul.
Les résultats couvrent la France métropolitaine et La Réunion.

### Base Tous Salariés (BTS)

Le champ correspond aux salariés du privé, y compris alternants,
                     stagiaires et bénéficiaires de contrats aidés, hors salariés de l’agriculture
                     et des particuliers employeurs.

### Système d’information sur la démographie d’entreprises (Side)

Les indicateurs portent sur les créations et les stocks
                     d’entreprises et d’établissements de l’ensemble des activités
                     productives et marchandes non agricoles. Ce champ inclut les activités
                     financières.
Quand on parle d’entreprises, tous les dénombrements portent en
                     réalité sur des unités légales pour cette source. Lorsqu’une unité
                     légale comprend plusieurs établissements, elle est localisée à son
                     siège.
Le nombre de créations d’entreprises ou d’établissements
                     correspond au nombre d’unités légales ou d’établissements créés au cours
                     de l’année N.
Le nombre d’entreprises ou d’établissements de l’année N
                     correspond au nombre d’unités légales ou d’établissements économiquement
                     actifs en N.

### Fichier localisé des rémunérations et de l’emploi salarié (Flores)

Le dispositif Flores (Fichier localisé des rémunérations et de
                     l’emploi salarié) couvre les établissements ayant employé au moins un
                     salarié pendant l’année, en France. Dans cette base
                     communale, les données mises à disposition sont par ailleurs restreintes
                     aux établissements actifs en fin d’année (dernière semaine de décembre),
                     ce qui exclut les établissements qui ont cessé leur activité en cours
                     d’année.
L’effectif salarié en fin d’année correspond au nombre de postes
                     présents la dernière semaine de décembre dans l’établissement employeur.
                     L’effectif en fin d’année de certains établissements peut donc être nul,
                     si le ou les personnes salariées pendant l’année n’étaient plus en
                     emploi fin décembre.
Flores couvre l’ensemble de l’emploi salarié, quel que soit le
                     secteur d’activité et le type d’employeur (public ou privé, y compris
                     les particuliers employeurs). Sont exclus du champ les établissements
                     relevant du ministère des Armées (personnels militaires comme civils).

### Base permanente des équipements (BPE)

La base permanente des équipements (BPE) est une base à vocation
                     statistique. Elle répertorie un large éventail d’équipements et de
                     services, marchands ou non, accessibles au public sur l’ensemble de la
                     France au 1ᵉʳ janvier de chaque année.
La base permanente des équipements (BPE) est un dispositif
                     alimenté par différentes sources : [sources
                        utilisées par la BPE](/fr/metadonnees/source/operation/s2216/processus-statistique).

### Tourisme

Le champ porte sur les hôtels de tourisme, classés ou pas, de
                     plus de 5
                     chambres et sur les campings de plus de 10 emplacements, classés ou pas,
                     y compris les
                     campings résidentiels. Il porte également sur les autres hébergements
                     collectifs
                     touristiques.

The Paris metropolitan area ([French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_language): Aire urbaine de Paris) is a [statistical area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Functional_area_(France)) that describes the reach of commuter movement to and from [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris), [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France) and its surrounding suburbs.

## Overview
[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Paris_metropolitan_area&action=edit&section=1)]
In 2020, France's national [INSEE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institut_national_de_la_statistique_et_des_études_économiques) statistical bureau introduced the concept "aire d'attraction d'une ville" ([functional area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Functional_area_(France))), replacing the former "aire urbaine" ([urban area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_area_(France))).[[2]](#cite_note-defaav-2) A functional area consists of an urban cluster[[3]](#cite_note-3) and the surrounding commuting zone.[[2]](#cite_note-defaav-2) This concept is consistent with the [functional urban area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larger_urban_zone) as defined by [Eurostat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurostat).[[4]](#cite_note-4)
Created and used from 1996 by France's national INSEE statistical bureau to match international demographic standards,[[5]](#cite_note-Hatier-5) the aire urbaine (literally: 'urban area') was a statistical unit that described the suburban development around centres of urban growth.[[6]](#cite_note-6) In 2011, the INSEE reclassified its largest aires urbaines into aires métropolitaines (literally: metropolitan areas) and grandes aires urbaines ('large urban areas').[[7]](#cite_note-INSEE-7) With this change, the Paris metropolitan area became the largest in France.[[8]](#cite_note-rang_AU-8)
In France, use of the term 'Paris metropolitan area' is limited to demographic and statistical studies, and, to date, it is not used in economic statistics — the traditional administrative subdivisions commune, département, and région are still referenced for this — though the media will employ it when referring to the electoral tendencies of France's largest cities[[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed)]. In 2010 the government passed a law that invited France's largest city 'metropoles' to work together as an intercommunitary entities (more or less described by the INSEE concept),[[9]](#cite_note-9) but the lack of response by the following year moved the government to make the cooperation for many of France's largest cities obligatory, and Paris became a case study all on its own.[[10]](#cite_note-10)
This latter initiative created the "[Métropole du Grand Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Paris)" (official translation: 'Greater Paris metropolitan authority'), a Paris-centred intercommunal cooperation effort enacted from January 1, 2016.[[11]](#cite_note-metropolegrandparis.fr-11) The territory it covers is much smaller than the INSEE 'Paris metropolitan area' statistical area: it includes Paris, its neighbouring three departments (or '[petite couronne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Île-de-France#Petite_Couronne)'), and a few bordering communes in the departments beyond.[[12]](#cite_note-Carte_des_territoires-12)

## Extent
[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Paris_metropolitan_area&action=edit&section=2)]Map showing the extent of the Paris metropolitan area at the 1999 census, when it included 1,584 [communes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communes_of_France) and covered 14,518 km2.[False-color](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/False_color) satellite image of the Parisian metropolitan area.
As of 2022, the INSEE statistical [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris) metropolitan area covers 1,929 communes.[[13]](#cite_note-cog-13) With its 18,941 km2 (7,313 sq mi), it extends significantly beyond Paris' administrative [Île-de-France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Île-de-France) [region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regions_of_France) (12,012 km2 (4,638 sq mi)).[[14]](#cite_note-compar-14) Outside the Île-de-France region, it covers part of the departments [Aisne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aisne), [Aube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aube), [Eure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eure), [Eure-et-Loir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eure-et-Loir), [Loiret](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loiret), [Marne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marne_(department)), [Oise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oise), [Seine-Maritime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seine-Maritime) and [Yonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonne).[[13]](#cite_note-cog-13)
The Paris metropolitan area expands at each population census due to the rapid population growth in the Paris area. New [communes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communes_of_France) (municipalities) surrounding Paris are included when they meet the commuter threshold required. At the 1968 census, the earliest date for which population figures were retrospectively computed for French aire urbaines, the Paris metropolitan area had 8,368,459 inhabitants in an area that only encompassed 279 communes in central Île-de-France.[[15]](#cite_note-Julien-15)
By the 1999 census the Paris metropolitan area was slightly larger than Île-de-France and had 11,174,743 inhabitants in 14,518 km2. At the 2010 revision, the aire urbaine of Paris had 1,750 communes.[[16]](#cite_note-meta-16)

#
Insee Flash Ile-de-France ·
               Octobre 2024 · n° 95Ville de Paris : un portrait de ses habitants

Amine Gomri, Nathalie Morer, Karl Pancarte (Insee)

Caractérisée par la densité de population la plus élevée de France, Paris compte 2,1
               millions d’habitants en 2024, soit 17 % de la population francilienne sur moins de
               1 % du territoire régional. Ses habitants sont plus âgés en moyenne que ceux de la
               métropole du Grand Paris et les cadres sont surreprésentés au sein de la population
               active. Le niveau de vie médian à Paris, comme dans les Hauts-de-Seine, est le plus
               élevé de France. Toutefois, de fortes inégalités sont présentes et la part de la population
               des ménages parisiens vivant sous le seuil de pauvreté atteint 15,6 %, contre 14,9 %
               en France métropolitaine. Malgré ses nombreux atouts en matière d’infrastructures
               et sa renommée internationale, la capitale française voit sa population diminuer depuis
               plusieurs années. Si les tendances démographiques actuelles se poursuivaient, Paris
               compterait, en 2040, 82 000 habitants de moins qu’en 2020.

## Paris perd des habitants depuis plusieurs décennies

Capitale de la France, Paris accueille 17 % de la population francilienne sur moins
                     de 1 % du territoire régional. Avec 19 900 habitants au km², la densité de population
                     y est la plus élevée de France. Selon les estimations de population les plus récentes,
                     en 2024, 2 087 600 personnes habitent à Paris, soit 45 500 de moins que trois ans
                     plus tôt. Cette baisse démographique s’inscrit dans une tendance enclenchée dès les
                     années 1950-1960. Ainsi, de 1968 à 1999, la population parisienne diminue de 0,6 %
                     en moyenne par an (soit 15 000 habitants de moins chaque année), avant de repartir
                     à la hausse au cours des années 2000 (+0,5 %, soit +10 800 habitants par an). La population
                     parisienne se replie à nouveau entre 2010 et 2015 (-0,3 %, soit -7 500 habitants par
                     an). Sur la période récente, de 2015 à 2021, Paris perd en moyenne 12 200 habitants
                     chaque année, soit 0,6 % de sa population. Ainsi, en 2021, Paris représente 30 % de
                     la population de l’ensemble des communes de la métropole du Grand Paris (MGP) contre
                     39 % en 1968.
Les évolutions démographiques à Paris s’expliquent par un solde migratoire négatif. À l’exception des années 2000, le solde naturel excédentaire ne suffit pas à compenser le déficit lié aux migrations résidentielles,
                     les arrivées sur Paris depuis la province ou l’étranger étant nettement inférieures
                     aux départs de la capitale. De 2015 à 2021, l’excès des naissances sur les décès contribue
                     à faire augmenter la population de 0,6 % chaque année mais, à l’inverse, le déficit
                     migratoire la fait diminuer de 1,2 %. Le solde migratoire est déficitaire pour toutes
                     les classes d’âge, à l’exception de celle des 18-24 ans, ce qui traduit des arrivées
                     importantes chaque année de jeunes actifs et d’étudiants à Paris.

## Une population parisienne plus âgée

Paris n’échappe pas au vieillissement de la population observé dans la métropole du
                     Grand Paris et sur l’ensemble du territoire national. La présence des seniors y est
                     même un peu plus forte : 23 % de la population parisienne est âgée de 60 ans ou plus
                     contre 20 % dans la MGP. A contrario, les enfants y sont proportionnellement moins
                     nombreux : 13 % des Parisiens ont moins de 15 ans, soit près de 5 points de moins
                     que dans la MGP (18 %). En revanche, les jeunes de 15 à 29 ans représentent près du
                     quart de la population parisienne (21 % pour la MGP). L’âge moyen des Parisiens est
                     de 40,3 ans contre 38,3 ans pour les habitants de la MGP.
Près des deux tiers des Parisiens de 15 ans ou plus sont actifs, soit en emploi soit au chômage, tandis que 18 % sont retraités et 18 %, sans activité.
                     Comparativement à la France et à la MGP, Paris se caractérise par une proportion bien
                     plus élevée de cadres et professions intellectuelles supérieures au sein de la population
                     active de 15 à 64 ans alors que les ouvriers et les employés y sont proportionnellement
                     moins présents ([figure 1](#figure1)). Cette prédominance, qui se renforce depuis plusieurs années, reflète notamment
                     le niveau de diplôme plus élevé à Paris : la moitié des actifs parisiens en emploi
                     (52 %) ont un diplôme d’enseignement supérieur de niveau Bac+5 ou plus. C’est 1,7
                     fois plus qu’en Île-de-France (30 %) et trois fois plus qu’au niveau national (17 %).
Les actifs parisiens travaillent très majoritairement dans la métropole du Grand Paris.
                     Ainsi, près des deux tiers occupent un emploi à Paris même et un quart dans les autres
                     communes de la MGP, dont principalement celles situées à la périphérie de Paris. Pour
                     se rendre sur leur lieu de travail, les Parisiens privilégient, à plus de 60 %, les
                     transports en commun. La proximité de leur lieu de travail et la densité du maillage
                     des transports collectifs en favorisent l’utilisation, et de façon plus marquée que
                     dans le reste de la MGP. Les mobilités douces (marche, trottinette, vélo...) progressent
                     régulièrement alors que la place de la voiture décroît depuis les années 1990 dans
                     la capitale. En 2021, à peine un ménage parisien sur trois est équipé d’au moins une
                     voiture. C’est une proportion deux fois moindre que pour l’ensemble des ménages résidant
                     dans la région.

## La moitié des ménages parisiens constitués d’une personne seule

À Paris, le nombre moyen de personnes composant un ménage s’établit à 1,85 en 2021.
                     Il est le plus élevé dans les 8e et 19e arrondissements et le plus faible dans les arrondissements centraux. Nettement inférieure
                     à la moyenne de la MGP (2,16), la taille moyenne des ménages à Paris reflète leur
                     structure, avec une part accrue des personnes seules et des couples sans enfant et
                     une proportion plus faible de familles avec enfant(s), et en particulier des familles
                     nombreuses ([figure 2](#figure2)). Ainsi, un ménage parisien sur deux est constitué d’une seule personne.
Près de 14 % des logements sont suroccupés, c’est-à-dire que le nombre de pièces y
                     est inférieur au besoin correspondant à la taille du ménage qui l’occupe. Ce taux
                     de suroccupation est proche de celui observé dans l’ensemble de la MGP, mais il est
                     plus important que dans d’autres grandes capitales régionales comme Marseille, Lyon
                     ou Toulouse. De manière générale, en comparaison avec l’ensemble de la MGP et ces
                     grandes villes, le parc de logements se caractérise par une surreprésentation des
                     logements de petite taille, d’une ou deux pièces, et une plus faible présence de grands
                     logements. Par ailleurs, les ménages parisiens sont moins souvent propriétaires de
                     leur logement (33 % contre 39 % dans la MGP), les deux tiers étant locataires du parc
                     privé ou social. Les logements occupés par des ménages représentent 81 % du parc ;
                     les autres logements sont, à parts presque égales, vacants ou des résidences secondaires
                     ou utilisés une partie de l’année pour des raisons professionnelles.

## Niveaux de vie : un territoire contrasté

Paris est, avec les Hauts-de-Seine, le département où le niveau de vie médian est le plus élevé en France. En 2021, la moitié des ménages parisiens ont un niveau
                     de vie supérieur à 29 730 euros, soit 2 480 euros par mois. Celui-ci est supérieur
                     au niveau de vie médian francilien (25 210 euros, soit 2 100 euros par mois). Les
                     arrondissements aux niveaux de vie médians les plus élevés se situent à l’ouest, avec
                     en tête les 7e et 8e arrondissements. A contrario, ceux où il est le plus bas sont les arrondissements
                     du nord-est parisien, le 19e étant l’arrondissement au niveau de vie médian le plus faible.
Paris est un territoire de contrastes avec une forte hétérogénéité des revenus : les
                     10 % des habitants les plus pauvres ont un niveau de vie au moins six fois moins élevé
                     que le niveau de vie minimum des 10 % les plus riches. Néanmoins, la moitié de la
                     population parisienne vit dans des quartiers qualifiés de socialement mixtes, c’est-à-dire
                     où la répartition par niveau de vie se rapproche de celle observée sur l’ensemble
                     de la MGP. Ces quartiers sont majoritairement situés dans le croissant est parisien.
En 2021, 15,6 % de la population des ménages parisiens vit sous le seuil de pauvreté monétaire, correspondant à 1 150 euros par mois pour une personne seule. Ce taux de pauvreté
                     est inférieur à celui de la MGP (18,3 %), mais supérieur à celui de la France métropolitaine
                     (14,9 %). Les situations des ménages parisiens vivant sous le seuil de pauvreté monétaire
                     sont diverses et peuvent être segmentées selon six profils. Ce sont des ménages retraités
                     (22 % d’entre eux), des ménages insérés sur le marché du travail, mais aux revenus
                     insuffisants (20 %) ou des ménages non insérés sur le marché du travail, que les personnes
                     de référence aient moins de 30 ans (14 %) ou soient locataires du parc privé (21 %),
                     du parc social (16 %) ou propriétaires (7 %).

## Des tendances démographiques qui pourraient se renforcer

D’ici 2040, si les tendances démographiques récentes se poursuivaient, la population
                     parisienne continuerait de diminuer pour atteindre 2 064 000 habitants. À la différence
                     de Paris, tous les autres départements franciliens verraient leur population poursuivre
                     leur croissance jusqu’en 2040. La décroissance démographique parisienne serait liée
                     à un solde migratoire déficitaire qui resterait important. Bien que positif, l’excédent
                     naturel baisserait progressivement sur la période, sous l’effet notamment de la hausse
                     des décès liée à l’arrivée des générations issues du baby-boom aux âges de grande
                     mortalité. La part des plus jeunes (moins de 15 ans) continuerait de diminuer et le
                     vieillissement de la population se poursuivrait ([figure 3](#figure3)). En 2040, Paris serait l’un des départements franciliens où la part des personnes
                     de 75 ans ou plus serait la plus élevée (12 %).

## Définitions

Le solde migratoire sur un territoire est la différence entre le nombre d’arrivées et le nombre de départs
                           au cours d'une période.

Le solde naturel est la différence entre le nombre de naissances et le nombre de décès enregistrés
                           au cours d'une période. On parle d'accroissement naturel ou d'excédent naturel lorsque
                           le nombre de naissances est supérieur à celui des décès.

La population active regroupe les personnes en emploi et les personnes au chômage. Les personnes sans
                           activité regroupent les étudiants ou élèves, stagiaires non rémunérés, hommes ou femmes
                           au foyer, les retraités et autres inactifs

Le niveau de vie du ménage est égal à son revenu disponible – revenu fiscal déclaré net des impôts
                           directs auquel s’ajoutent les prestations sociales – divisé par le nombre d’unités
                           de consommation (UC) : 1 pour le premier adulte, 0,5 par autre personne de 14 ans
                           ou plus et 0,3 par enfant de moins de 14 ans. Le niveau de vie médian est tel que la moitié de la population a un niveau de vie inférieur et l’autre moitié,
                           un niveau de vie supérieur.

Pauvreté monétaire : un individu (ou un ménage) est considéré comme pauvre lorsqu'il vit dans un ménage
                           dont le niveau de vie est inférieur au seuil de pauvreté. En France et en Europe,
                           le seuil est le plus souvent fixé à 60 % du niveau de vie médian.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

For cities within the European Union, see [List of cities in the European Union by population within city limits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_the_European_Union_by_population_within_city_limits).Istanbul view
This list ranks European cities by population within city limits. The largest cities in [Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europe) have official populations of over one million inhabitants within their [city boundaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_limits). These rankings are based on populations contained within city administrative boundaries, as opposed to [urban areas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_urban_areas_in_Europe) or [metropolitan areas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_metropolitan_areas_in_Europe), which necessarily have larger populations than the cities at their core.
The limits of a [city proper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_proper) can differ greatly from the size of the city's urban area, so the figures in this list may not give an accurate view of the comparative population of different urban areas and should be treated with caution. For example, the [Paris metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_metropolitan_area) is the fourth most populous in Europe, but the strict definition of the administrative limits of the [City of Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris) results in a far lower population.
